newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot sees big changes in its winter schedule.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot sees big changes in its winter schedule.

text.p: Russian flagship carrier Aeroflot will drop some of its international routes from October 27 as they are not profitable, a senior airline official said on Thursday.

Aeroflot's chief of North America department Alexander Voitsekhovitch told a news conference the airline would drop regular flights from Moscow to Panama, Nagoya in Japan, Bahrain, Shanghai in China and Almaty, the capital of Kazakhstan.
He also said the company would cut the number of its regular flights from Moscow to Berlin and Venice.
"We will re-start Moscow-Havana regular 12-hour non-stop flights on Saturdays, operating an Ilyushin-96-300 jet," Voitsekhovitch said.

He also said Aeroflot was in talks with Norilsk Nikel, the largest northern Russian metallurgical combine, about regular charters to Havana for workers at the plant. "We hope to carry 150 tourists from Norilsk to Cuba monthly," he said.
Aeroflot deputy commercial director Nikolai Lebedev said the company planned to launch Baku-Kuwait, Tashkent-Tehran regular flights jointly with Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan airlines.

Meanwhile, Aeroflot said in statetment that would start a twice weekly service from Moscow to Washington and Miami operating A-310 jets. The company will add a flight to its twice weekly service from Moscow to Chicago operating a Boeing-767.
The company also will operate non-stop flights between Moscow and Delhi three times a week.

In all, the company plans to operate 352 international flights per week to 94 countries around the world from the end of October. A further 100 international flights will be operated by others Russian airlines under the Aeroflot flag from St Petersburg, Khabarovsk, Irkutsk, Murmansk and Vladivistok.

Aeroflot carried 3.5 million passengers in 1995, up from three million the previous year and 70,000 tonnes of cargo and mail up from 60,800 tonnes in 1994. The company hopes to carry 3.8 million passengers this year.
